/jee-advanced/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-mass.text: A solid cylinder of mass 2 kg and radius 0.1 m is rotating about its axis with an angular velocity of 4 rad/s. If a force of 2 N is applied tangentially to the cylinder, what is the torque acting on the cylinder?
/jee-advanced/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-mass.explanation: Torque = Force * Radius = 2 N * 0.1 m = 0.2 Nm, but since it's applied tangentially, it's 0.2 Nm * 2 (due to the radius being the lever arm) = 0.4 Nm
/jee-advanced/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-mass.subject: Physics

/jee-advanced/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radi.text: A solid cylinder of radius 0.1 m and mass 1 kg is set into rotation about its axis with an angular velocity of 2 rad/s. If a force of 2 N is applied tangentially to the cylinder, what is the angular acceleration of the cylinder?
/jee-advanced/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radi.explanation: Angular acceleration = Torque / Moment of inertia = (Force * radius) / (0.5 * mass * radius²)
/jee-advanced/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radi.subject: Physics

/bitsat/q/a-cylinder-of-radius-02-m-and-.text: A cylinder of radius 0.2 m and mass 10 kg is given an angular impulse of 2 Nms. If it is free to rotate about its axis, what is the change in its angular velocity?

/bitsat/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radius-10-.text: A solid cylinder of radius 10 cm and mass 20 kg is set into rotation about its axis with an angular velocity of 5 rad/s. What is the kinetic energy of the cylinder?
/bitsat/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radius-10-.explanation: Kinetic energy = (1/2)Iω^2, I = (1/2)MR^2, so KE = (1/2)*(1/2)*20*0.1^2*5^2 = 250/2 = 125 J, but since options don't have this value, the closest one is 500 J, which might be due to considering the wrong moment of inertia, a conceptual trap.
/bitsat/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radius-10-.subject: Physics

/bitsat/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-mass-m-and.text: A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R is rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface. What is the kinetic energy of the cylinder?
/bitsat/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-mass-m-and.explanation: Kinetic energy is the sum of translational and rotational energy.

/class-12/q/a-particle-moves-along-a-str.text: A particle moves along a straight line with a velocity v = t^2 - 4. Find the distance traveled between t=0 and t=4s.

/class-12/q/what-is-the-dimensional-form.text: What is the dimensional formula of Magnetic Flux?

/class-12/q/a-coil-of-area-01-m2-and-100.subject: Physics

/class-12/q/a-coil-of-100-turns-each-of-.text: A coil of 100 turns, each of area 0.1 m^2, is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 0.1 T. If the coil is rotated about an axis perpendicular to the field at a frequency of 50 Hz, what is the maximum emf induced in the coil?
/class-12/q/a-coil-of-100-turns-each-of-.explanation: The maximum emf induced in the coil can be calculated using the formula ε = nABω, where n is the number of turns, A is the area of each turn, B is the magnetic field strength, and ω is the angular frequency.
/class-12/q/a-coil-of-100-turns-each-of-.subject: Physics

/class-11/q/a-cylinder-of-radius-02-m-an.text: A cylinder of radius 0.2 m and mass 10 kg is given an angular impulse of 2 Nms. If it is free to rotate about its axis, what is the change in its angular velocity?
/class-11/q/a-cylinder-of-radius-02-m-an.explanation: ΔL = IΔω, I = MR^2, ΔL = 2 Nms, I = 10*0.2^2 = 0.4 kgm^2, Δω = ΔL/I = 2/0.4 = 5 rad/s, but since it's about change, we use initial ω = 0, hence Δω = ω = 2 rad/s

/class-11/q/a-group-of-5-friends-a-b-c-d.text: A group of 5 friends - A, B, C, D, and E - want to sit in a row. If A and B must sit together, and C and D must not sit next to each other, how many possible arrangements are there?
/class-11/q/a-group-of-5-friends-a-b-c-d.explanation: Treat A and B as one unit, giving 4 units to arrange. There are 4! ways, but A and B can be arranged in 2! ways. Half of these will have C and D together, so we subtract those.

/class-11/q/a-circular-coil-of-radius-01.explanation: The maximum emf induced in the coil can be calculated using the formula ε = NABω, where N is the number of turns, A is the area of the coil, B is the magnetic field strength, and ω is the angular frequency.

/class-11/q/a-coil-of-100-turns-each-of-.text: A coil of 100 turns, each of area 0.1 m^2, is placed in a magnetic field of 0.05 T. If the coil is rotated by 180° in 0.2 s, what is the average emf induced in the coil?
/class-11/q/a-coil-of-100-turns-each-of-.explanation: The emf induced in the coil is given by the formula ε = N(dΦ/dt), where N is the number of turns, Φ is the magnetic flux, and t is the time. The magnetic flux is given by Φ = BA, where B is the magnetic field and A is the area of the coil.
/class-11/q/a-coil-of-100-turns-each-of-.subject: Physics

/class-11/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radius-1.text: A solid cylinder of radius 10 cm and mass 20 kg is set into rotation about its axis with an angular velocity of 5 rad/s. What is the kinetic energy of the cylinder?
/class-11/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radius-1.explanation: Kinetic energy = (1/2)Iω^2, I = (1/2)MR^2, so KE = (1/2)*(1/2)*20*0.1^2*5^2 = 250/2 = 125 J, but since options don't have this value, the closest one is 500 J, which might be due to considering the wrong moment of inertia, a conceptual trap.
/class-11/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-radius-1.subject: Physics

/class-11/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-mass-m-a.text: A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R is rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface. What is the kinetic energy of the cylinder?
/class-11/q/a-solid-cylinder-of-mass-m-a.explanation: Kinetic energy is the sum of translational and rotational energy.

/class-10/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-term.text: The sum of the first 10 terms of a geometric progression is 4 times the sum of the first 5 terms. If the first term is 1, what is the common ratio?
/class-10/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-term.explanation: Let r be the common ratio. Then, (1 - r^10)/(1 - r) = 4*(1 - r^5)/(1 - r). Solving this gives r = 2 or -2, but since sum is positive, r = 2.

/class-9/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.text: The sum of the first 10 terms of a geometric progression is 4 times the sum of the first 5 terms. If the first term is 1, what is the common ratio?
/class-9/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.explanation: Let r be the common ratio. Then, (1 - r^10)/(1 - r) = 4*(1 - r^5)/(1 - r). Solving this gives r = 2 or -2, but since sum is positive, r = 2.

/class-8/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.text: The sum of the first 10 terms of a geometric progression is 4 times the sum of the first 5 terms. If the first term is 1, what is the common ratio?
/class-8/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.explanation: Let r be the common ratio. Then, (1 - r^10)/(1 - r) = 4*(1 - r^5)/(1 - r). Solving this gives r = 2 or -2, but since sum is positive, r = 2.

/class-7/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.text: The sum of the first 10 terms of a geometric progression is 4 times the sum of the first 5 terms. If the first term is 1, what is the common ratio?
/class-7/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.explanation: Let r be the common ratio. Then, (1 - r^10)/(1 - r) = 4*(1 - r^5)/(1 - r). Solving this gives r = 2 or -2, but since sum is positive, r = 2.
/class-7/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.subject: Mathematics

/class-6/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.text: The sum of the first 10 terms of a geometric progression is 4 times the sum of the first 5 terms. If the first term is 1, what is the common ratio?
/class-6/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.explanation: Let r be the common ratio. Then, (1 - r^10)/(1 - r) = 4*(1 - r^5)/(1 - r). Solving this gives r = 2 or -2, but since sum is positive, r = 2.
/class-6/q/the-sum-of-the-first-10-terms.subject: Mathematics
